subject: Correlated effects IID vs Autogressive and Random Walks

messages.author: f120a4140c97c18f
messages.subject: Correlated effects IID vs Autogressive and Random Walks
parts:
Dear,

I am trying to fit a model finding the relationship between fish otolith increment and fish age with year random intercept (increments of the same year higher/lower than of another year) and year-level random slope on age (increment~age slope of different years are different).

This is the syntax using iid2d to have correlated effects of year random intercept and year-level random slope on age (reference: chap 3.3.8 of this book https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-mixed.html#correlated-effects-iidd-models):

increment ~ age + f(year.id, model = "iid2d", n = n.year*2) + f(year.id.age, age, copy = " year.id")

where:

-         - year.id is the id of year to estimate year random intercept: 1-141

-         - n.year is the number of year: 141

-         - year.id.age is the id of to estimate year-level random slope on age: 142-282

I wonder if it is possible to fit the model with correlated effects of year random intercept and year-level random slope on age using autogressive (ar) or random walks (rw)?  

 

For the moment, I see that I can fit a model with the following syntax, but the year random intercept and year-level random slope on age will not be correlated:

increment ~ age + f(year.id, model = "ar1") + f(year.id.copy, age, model = “ar1”)

where:

-         - year.id is the id of year to estimate year random intercept: 1-141

-         - year.id.copy (exactly the same as year.id) is the id of to estimate year-level random slope on age: 1-141

Thank you for your help. If there is anything not clear in my question due to my limited experience, please mention it so I can clarify.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Correlated effects IID vs Autogressive and Random Walks
parts:
you can doit the other way around, iid2d x ar1.

I think this is what you want, please check. It was quickly done but at
least it estimate back the simulated model. for simplicity I fixed the
precision in the observation process.

H


library(mvtnorm)
n <- 3000
cor <- 0.7
phi <- 0.9
S <- matrix(c(1, cor, cor, 1), 2, 2)
eps <- rmvnorm(n, sigma = S)

x <- matrix(NA, n, 2)
x[1, ]<- eps[1, ]
for(i in 2:n) {
x[i, ] <- phi * x[i-1, ] + eps[i, ]
}
x <- x * sqrt(1-phi^2)

age <- rnorm(n)
s <- 0.1
y <- 1 + x[, 1] + age * x[, 2] + rnorm(n, sd = s)

r <- inla(
y ~ 1 + f(idx, model = "iid2d", n = 2,
group = time, control.group = list(model = "ar1")) +
f(idx.age, age, copy = "idx", group = time),
data = data.frame(y,
idx = rep(1, n),
idx.age = rep(2, n),
time = 1:n),
family = "gaussian",
control.family = list(
hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1/s^2),
fixed = TRUE))))

summary(r)

Dear Havard,

Thank you so much again for your help. I want to ask how should I interpret the results.
This is the summary of the hyperparameters of the simulated model above (at n = 1000, there is something wrong when I tried n = 3000):

Model hyperparameters: mean sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant mode Precision for idx (component 1) 1.168 0.133 0.924 1.162 1.447 1.152 Precision for idx (component 2) 1.230 0.133 0.984 1.225 1.507 1.217 Rho1:2 for idx 0.705 0.030 0.644 0.706 0.760 0.707 GroupRho for idx 0.887 0.012 0.863 0.887 0.908 0.888

My guess is that: 
Precision for idx (component 1): precision of x[,1] or random intercept
Precision for idx (component 2) : precision of x[,2] or age slope
Rho1:2 for idx: rho to estimate the correlation of random intercept and age slope
GroupRho for idx: rho to estimate autoregressive (ar1) correlation. However, there is only 1 value so this means the ar1 for intercept and ar1 for age slope have the same rho/correlation value?

I hope you can help me with this.

Best regards,
Tuan Anh
